questions.stem: Why does pepsin work effectively in the stomach but not in the small intestine?

options.text: Pepsin is broken down by bile in the small intestine
Pepsin needs an acidic pH (around pH 2) found in the stomach, but the small intestine is alkaline
The small intestine does not contain any proteins to digest
The small intestine is too warm for pepsin to function

questions.explanation: Pepsin has an optimum pH of about 2 (acidic), which matches the conditions in the stomach due to hydrochloric acid. In the alkaline small intestine, pepsin is denatured and cannot function.
